description: CALBRACE: IMPLEMENTING AND EVALUATING ADAPTATION STRATEGIES THAT PROTECT AND PROMOTE HUMAN HEALTH - THE CALIFORNIA DEPARTMENT OF PUBLIC HEALTH (CDPH) OFFICE OF HEALTH EQUITY’S CLIMATE CHANGE AND HEALTH EQUITY SECTION (CCHES) AND THE CALIFORNIA BUILDING RESILIENCE AGAINST CLIMATE EFFECTS (CALBRACE) PROJECT WILL BUILD INFRASTRUCTURE TO SUPPORT AN ALL-OF-CALIFORNIA EFFORT FOR CLIMATE AND HEALTH ADAPTION PLANNING, ACTION, AND EVALUATION WITH DATA, TOOLS, COMMUNICATIONS, ENGAGEMENT, AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, TRIBES, COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, STATE AGENCIES, AND CDPH PROGRAMS. THIS EFFORT WILL BUILD RESILIENCE TO THE HEALTH IMPACTS OF HEAT, WILDFIRE, WILDFIRE SMOKE, DROUGHT, AND OTHER CLIMATE-RELATED HAZARDS THROUGH THESE OVERARCHING STRATEGIES: 1) COLLABORATION WITH STAKEHOLDERS TO CREATE A CLIMATE IMPACT COMPENDIUM THAT INCLUDES DATA ON LOCAL CLIMATE PROJECTIONS, HEALTH EFFECTS, SOCIAL DETERMINANTS OF HEALTH, AND ADAPTIVE CAPACITY; 2) PLANNING, IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION OF ADAPTATION ACTIONS THAT ADDRESS THE THREATS IDENTIFIED IN THE COMPENDIUM; AND 3) USE AND DISSEMINATION OF EVALUATION RESULTS TO IMPROVE ACTIONS AND UNDERSTANDING OF EFFECTIVE CLIMATE RESILIENCE ADAPTATIONS IN PUBLIC HEALTH AND RELATED SECTORS. CALBRACE WILL INCREASE EFFORTS TO UNDERSTAND AND REDUCE THE HEALTH EFFECTS ASSOCIATED WITH CLIMATE-RELATED EVENTS AND EXPOSURES. KEY OUTCOMES WILL BE STRONGER PARTNERSHIPS, INCREASED KNOWLEDGE OF ADAPTATION ACTIONS AND AN ENHANCED EVIDENCE BASE FOR EFFECTIVE CLIMATE AND HEALTH ADAPTATION ACTIONS. SUPPORT FROM CLIMATE EPIDEMIOLOGISTS FROM UC SAN DIEGO AND UC DAVIS WILL ADD SCIENTIFIC RIGOR GUIDING THE CLIMATE COMPENDIUM CONTENT AND ANALYSIS TO PRIORITIZE ACTIVITIES AND DIRECT RESOURCES TO BUILD CLIMATE RESILIENCE FOR AND WITH COMMUNITIES WITH HIGH SUSCEPTIBILITY TO CLIMATE HAZARDS AND HISTORICAL AND CONTINUING DISINVESTMENT. WITH STATE AGENCY PARTNERS, EVALUATION SPECIALISTS, REGIONAL NONPROFITS, TRIBES, AND TRIBE- SERVING PROVIDERS, SCIENTIFIC ACADEMIC ADVISORS, AND COMMUNITIES, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE LIVING COND ITIONS, INCREASE ADAPTIVE CAPACITY AND RESILIENCE, AND DISSEMINATE NEW EVIDENCE TO THE PUBLIC HEALTH FIELD AT THE NEXUS OF CLIMATE CHANGE, HEALTH, AND EQUITY.  CALBRACE SEEKS TO: 1) PROVIDE TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE TO LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS AND TRIBES/ TRIBAL HEALTH ORGANIZATIONS TO PLAN, IMPLEMENT, AND EVALUATE ACTIONS THAT DRIVE HEALTH AND EQUITY OUTCOMES WHILE REDUCING GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS. 2) CONSULT ON CLIMATE, HEALTH AND EQUITY IN SERVICE TO STATE AGENCIES’ CLIMATE-RELATED PLANS, POLICIES, AND INVESTMENTS; 3) DEVELOP A PILOT TRAINING AND TOOLS FOR A HEALTHY HOMES APPROACH WITH COMMUNITY HEALTH PROMOTER ORGANIZATIONS/ "PROMOTORES DE SALUD" TO EDUCATE AND REFER CLIENTS TO THE CALIFORNIA LOW-INCOME WEATHERIZATION PROGRAM (LIWP) AND HOME ENERGY EFFICIENCY UPGRADES TO REDUCE HEAT AND WILDFIRE SMOKE EXPOSURE; AND 4) SUPPORT THE TRIBAL CLIMATE PROJECT TO INCREASE ENGAGEMENT WITH AND TRAINING FOR THE STATE, COUNTIES, TRIBES, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS ON TRIBAL CLIMATE PRIORITIES AND POLICIES. ENGAGEMENT WITH COMMUNITIES, ORGANIZATIONS, LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS WILL INFORM THE ACTIVITIES AND PRODUCTS IN THE CLIMATE COMPENDIUM (CLIMATE CHANGE AND HEALTH EQUITY-RELATED DATA, MAPS, AND ADAPTATION PLANNING GUIDANCE). COMPONENTS FOR ADAPTATION ENHANCEMENT, MITIGATION AND DATA MODERNIZATION WILL ADD RIGOR AND STRENGTH TO IMPLEMENT AND SCALE UP KEY ACTIONS INCLUDING ADDING HEALTH INDICATORS TO THE CLIMATE CHANGE AND HEALTH VULNERABILITY INDICATORS FOR CALIFORNIA AND THE CCHVIZ WEB PLATFORM; FUND LOCAL HEALTH DEPARTMENTS, TRIBES, AND HEALTH PROMOTER ORGANIZATIONS; SUPPORT THE GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF PLANNING AND RESEARCH IN CREATING THE EQUITY FOCUSED VULNERABLE COMMUNITIES PLATFORM, UPDATE THE CALIFORNIA EMISSIONS ESTIMATOR MODEL (CALEEMOD), THE CALIFORNIA HEALTH ASSESSMENT TOOL AND THE CALBRACE ADAPTATION TOOLKIT. PRODUCTS, ACTIVITIES, PUBLICATIONS, AND EVALUATION FINDING

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: To bring public health and epidemiologic principles together to identify, clarify, and reduce the impact of complex environmental threats, including terrorist threats and natural disasters, on populations, domestic and foreign.  These programs and activities focus on safeguarding the health of people from environmental threats; providing leadership in the use of environmental health sciences-including environmental epidemiology, environmental sanitation, and laboratory sciences-to protect public health; and responding to issues and sharing solutions to environmental health problems worldwide.  To accomplish the above, the CDC: (1) conducts surveillance and investigations that increase the knowledge about the relation between human health and environmental threats; (2) uses this knowledge to develop national public health programs and policies to prevent or control public health problems; (3) plans, prepares, and responds to emergencies, including terrorist threats, technologic accidents, and natural disasters; (4) provides direct service delivery to partners engaged in environmental health services such as food, safety, rodent control, water quality, and sanitation; (5) develops and applies laboratory science to prevent disease and death caused by exposure to environmental chemicals and to improve the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of selected chronic diseases; (6) conducts Biomonitoring to assess individual human exposure to environmental chemicals by measuring them in human specimens (e.g. blood and urine); and, (7) conducts activities on emerging environmental threats such as climate change and the built environment.

cfda_info.cfda_objectives: To assist State and local health authorities and other health related organizations in controlling communicable diseases, chronic diseases and disorders, and other preventable health conditions. Investigations and evaluation of all methods of controlling or preventing disease and disability are carried out by providing epidemic aid, surveillance, technical assistance, consultation, and program support; and by providing leadership and coordination of joint national, State, and local efforts.
